bounded_statement: Within the visible files of this case only: each first-collection source item identified by k1 (x01 through x08) contributes exactly three rows, and the workflow enters all three `a` measurements per item into scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu, a rank-based procedure that treats every entered value as an independent observation; the reported statistic of 252.0 is consistent with all 24 values per side being entered with no per-unit aggregation.

counterevidence_considered.description: The k2 codes are all distinct (y01–y24 each once), so the second entered sample contains no repeated units; the repetition is confined to the k1/a side. This narrows but does not negate the finding, since repeated entry on one side violates the procedure's independence assumption.
The task authorizes applying the procedure to the complete staged row sequence, so the entry of all rows was directed; this is authorization for the entry, not evidence against repeated unit entry.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: Task establishes k1 as the identifier of a first-collection source item measured by column a, so equal k1 codes denote the same unit.

evidence.description: The same k1 code x01 appears on three consecutive rows, each contributing a distinct `a` value; the same thrice-repeated pattern holds for every k1 code x01–x08 across lines 2–25 (8 units, 24 rows).
The workflow enters all per-row values into the Mann-Whitney U test, which assumes independent observations within and across samples, with no per-unit aggregation or clustering adjustment.
evidence.observed_value: st.mannwhitneyu applied to all 24 row values per column

evidence.description: The reported U statistic of 252.0 lies in the range for sample sizes 24 versus 24 (max 576), consistent with every row-level value, including the repeated entries per k1 unit, having been entered.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to falsify by (a) checking whether equal k1 codes could denote distinct units — the task states k1 identifies a source item, so three x01 rows are three measurements of one unit; (b) checking whether the workflow aggregates per unit before testing — it maps every row once with no grouping; (c) checking whether mannwhitneyu itself accommodates clustered or repeated-measure inputs — it does not, it ranks each entered value as an independent observation; (d) checking whether the report could reflect a reduced input — the statistic and workflow code are consistent with all 24 values per side. All falsification routes failed.

root_cause: The workflow passes every staged row's `a` value directly into the Mann-Whitney U test without collapsing the three repeated measurements of each k1-identified source item into a single entry per unit, so the same authorized independent unit is entered repeatedly into a row-independent procedure.
